title: SkillLift: Learning Dense Rubrics from Sparse Oracles for Efficient Skill Evolution
abstract: arXiv:2609.15396v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM-based agents increasingly rely on persistent skills, i.e., reusable procedural prompts, to adapt without weight updates. Existing skill self-evolution methods directly revise skill text based on execution feedback, but each oracle evaluation requires a full agent rollout, creating a supervision bottleneck that confines search to failure-patching updates. Our key insight is that ranking is a smoother supervision target than absolute outcome regression: identifying which skill is better requires fewer oracle evaluations than predicting exact scores. Building on this insight, we propose SkillLift, which decouples skill search from oracle cost by learning an oracle-aligned rubric as a structured evaluation space. translated_title: SkillLift：从稀疏Oracle学习密集评分标准以实现高效技能演化
translated_abstract: 基于LLM的智能体越来越依赖持久化技能（即可复用的程序化提示）来在不更新权重的情况下实现适应。现有的技能自演化方法直接根据执行反馈修改技能文本，但每次oracle评估都需要完整的智能体执行过程，这造成了监督瓶颈，将搜索局限在失败修补式的更新上。我们的关键洞察是，排序是比绝对结果回归更平滑的监督目标：识别哪个技能更好所需的oracle评估次数要少于预测精确分数所需的次数。基于这一洞察，我们提出了SkillLift，它通过学习一个与oracle对齐的评分标准作为结构化评估空间，将技能搜索与oracle成本解耦。我们将该问题形式化为一个双层优化问题，并通过交替优化求解：内循环使用冻结的评分标准作为廉价替代品，在零oracle成本的情况下指导技能修订；外循环则调用少量oracle评估来对齐评分标准。
tldr: SkillLift通过学习与oracle对齐的密集评分标准作为廉价的结构化评估空间，将LLM智能体的技能搜索与昂贵的oracle评估解耦，从而实现更高效的技能自演化。
en_tdlr: SkillLift decouples skill search from costly oracle evaluations by learning a dense, oracle-aligned rubric as a cheap structured evaluation space, enabling more efficient self-evolution of LLM agent skills.
